newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE EUROYEN ENDS DOWN ON LONG LIQUIDATION.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE EUROYEN ENDS DOWN ON LONG LIQUIDATION.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract settled slightly lower on Wednesday, due to long liquidation, traders said.

"Everybody is long right now, and I think people just became a bit cautious ahead of the release of key U.S. indicators and decided to trim down their positions a bit," a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
The March's day session turnover was 41,702 contracts.
It moved in a range of 99.19 and 99.22.
The March fell to 99.19 in the early morning due to large-lot selling, traders said.
"Bids at 99.20 totalling 10,000 contracts were all hit by offers and triggered a fall in the March to 99.19 in the early morning," a trader for a brokerage house said.
But the March was later lifted off lows due to firmness in Japanese government bonds, traders said.
News in the afternoon that Mitsui Construction Co Ltd had submitted a restructuring plan was also supportive, they said.

Reports of financial trouble at debt-laden construction firms reinforce a view that interest rates are likely to be maintained at the current low levels for some time, and is positive for euroyen futures, a trust bank trader said.
Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd said that Mitsui Construction Co Ltd had submitted a restructuring plan and added that it was unlikely to reject the plan across-the board.
Mitsui Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd later said that it, Mitsui Trust and two other financial institutions belonging to the Mitsui group had decided to accept the restructuring plan.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market this morning, against a projected fund shortfall of 390 billion yen.
Traders said the key overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.47 percent on Wednesday, unchanged from Tuesday's weighted average.

About 10 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.58 percent. About 60 billion yen worth of the key two-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent and 10 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.53 percent.
